rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed apposition of a derivative is grammatically weak according to grammarians, though Abu Hayyan may reject that rule.
rows.anchor: نصوا على أن إبدال المشتق ضعيف

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan may not accept the claim that apposition of a derivative is weak.
rows.anchor: ولعل أبا حيان لا يسلم ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan allows جنات عدن as either complete apposition or explanatory apposition; لا يظلمون is parenthetical or circumstantial under either parse.
rows.anchor: جوز كون جنات عدن بدل كل وكذا جوز كونه عطف بيان

rows.speaker: الحسن، أبو حيوة، عيسى بن عمر، الأعمش، أحمد بن موسى عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: They read جنات عدن in the nominative plural; Abu Hayyan parses it as a predicate of an omitted subject, while others make it the subject followed by the relative clause.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن وابو حيوة وعيسى بن عمر والأعمش واحمد بن موسى عن أبى عمرو جنات عدن بالرفع

rows.speaker: الحسن بن حي، علي بن صالح، الأعمش
rows.claim: They read the singular accusative جنة عدن; this form is also found in the codex of Abdullah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن حي وعلى بن صالح جنة عدن بالنصب والأفراد ورويت عن الأعمش

rows.speaker: اليماني، الحسن، إسحاق الأزرق عن حمزة
rows.claim: They read the singular nominative جنة عدن, with an omitted pronoun referring back to the relative clause: the Merciful promised it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليمانى والحسن في رواية واسحق الأزرق عن حمزة ( جنة عدن ) بالرفع والأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Merciful signals that the promise and its fulfillment arise from the fullness of divine mercy.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الرحمة للايذان بأن وعدها وإنجازه لكمال سعة رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بالغيب can be circumstantial: the Gardens are unseen and absent from the servants, or the servants are absent from the Gardens and cannot see them.
rows.anchor: للملابسة وهي متعلقة بمضمر هو حال من العائد أو من عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بالغيب may instead express cause, meaning God promised the Gardens because the servants affirmed and believed in the unseen.
rows.anchor: لِلسببية وهي متعلقة بوعد أي وعدها إياهم بسبب تصديق الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed attachment of بالغيب to عباده meaning they worship God privately is judged weak.
rows.anchor: صلة عباده على معنى الذين يعبدونه سبحانه بالغيب أي في السر وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in إنه may refer to the Merciful, or be an impersonal pronoun announcing the clause.
rows.anchor: أي الرحمن وجوز كون الضمير للشان

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The promise is interpreted as its promised object, namely the Gardens; alternatively it means God's appointment generally, or the promise itself by metonymic usage.
rows.anchor: وهو الجنات كما روى عن ابن جريج أو موعده كائنا ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense كان conveys that the promise will certainly occur; مأتيا means the promisee will inevitably reach it, or that it comes, or that it is fulfilled as a favor.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بكان للايذان بتحقق الوقوع أي كان ذلك ( ماتيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لغو is futile talk, including sounds like birdsong; saying it is not heard in Paradise implies its people do not speak idly and teaches avoidance of idle talk here.
rows.anchor: فضول كلام لاطائل تحته بل هو جارمجرى اللغاء وهو صوت العصافير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets لغو as speech containing insults, so the verse means the people of Paradise do not abuse one another.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد تفسير اللغو بالكلام المشتمل على السب والمراد لا يتسابون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general meaning of futile speech is preferable to restricting the word to mutual insults.
rows.anchor: والتعميم أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of سلاما may be disconnected: inhabitants hear greetings from angels or one another, or speech free of defect and deficiency.
rows.anchor: لكن يسمعون تسليم الملائكة عليهم السلام عليهم أو تسليم بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be connected as praise phrased like blame; this hypothetical reading emphatically proves they hear no idle talk.
rows.anchor: وهو يفيد نفي سماع اللغو بالطريق البرهاني الاقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another connected reading, greetings seem unnecessary because Paradise has no harm, but they express honor and affection.
rows.anchor: وحيث أن أهل الجنة أغنياء عن ذلك إذ لا آفة فيها كان السلام لغوا بحسب الظاهر

rows.speaker: يحيى بن كثير
rows.claim: Arabs in his time usually ate once daily and called a person who managed two meals prosperous; the verse promises more abundant provision.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن يحيى ابن كثير قال : كانت العرب في زمانها انما لها أكلة واحدة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A similar explanation of the morning and evening provision is also reported from Hasan.
rows.anchor: وروى نحو ذلك عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Paradise has no morning or evening, the phrase may mean that provision is continuous; reports say its inhabitants tell night and day by curtains and doors opening or closing.
rows.anchor: المراد دوام رزقهم ودروره وإلا فليس في الجنة بكرة ولا عشى

rows.speaker: الحسن، أبو قلابة
rows.claim: A report transmitted through al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi says a man asked the Prophet whether Paradise has night because of this verse; he replied that it has no night, only light alternating between morning and evening, gifts at former prayer times, and angelic greetings.
rows.anchor: من طريق ابان عن الحسن وابى قلابه قالا : جاء رجل إلى رسول الله ( صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse begins a new statement to magnify Paradise and identify its people; the demonstrative is subject, Paradise its predicate, and the relative clause modifies it with an omitted object pronoun.
rows.anchor: استئناف جئ به لتعظيم شأن الجنة وتعيين أهلها

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reads نورثها, making explicit the omitted object pronoun referring to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وبذلك قرأ الأعمش

rows.speaker: الحسن، الأعرج، قتادة، رويس، حميد، ابن أبي عبلة، أبو حيوة، محبوب عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: They read نورث with an intensified ر; inheritance means preserving Paradise for the pious as the fruit of their piety, like an heir retaining an estate.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن والأعرج وقتادة ورويس وحميد وابن أبى عبلة وابو حيوة ومحبوب عن أبى عمرو ( نورث ) بفتح الواو وتشديد الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance is a metaphor for permanent possession, chosen because it is the most complete transfer of ownership, without cancellation, recovery, or annulment.
rows.anchor: فالايراث مستعار للبقاء واثاره على سائر ما يدل على ذلك كالبيع والهبة لأنه اتم انواع التمليك

rows.speaker: ابن شوذب
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits Ibn Shawdhab's view that everyone has a home and spouses in Paradise, and believers inherit dwellings of unbelievers at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبى حاتم عن ابن شوذب قال : ليس من أحد إلا وله في الجنة منزل وازواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unless supported by a Prophetic report, the view that believers inherit only some dwellings is weak: the wording indicates all Paradise, and inheritance suggests prior ownership rather than a hypothetical estate.
rows.anchor: أنه ضعيف لأنه يدل على أن بعض الجنة موروث والنظم الجليل يدل على انها كلها كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reply says the estate need only have existed conditionally for those who would have believed; most interpreters take servants in 19:61 as the pious but take them here more broadly.
rows.anchor: نعم اختار الأكثرون أن المراد من العباد هناك المتقون والمراد منهم هنا الأعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious person is glossed as one who believes and acts righteously; the verse does not prove that anyone else is absolutely barred from Paradise.
rows.anchor: والمراد من التقي من آمن وعمل صالحا على ما قيل ولا دلالة في الآية على أن غيره لا يدخل الجنة مطلقا

rows.speaker: داود بن أبي هند
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits Dawud ibn Abi Hind's interpretation that the pious person here is a monotheist.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبى حاتم عن داود بن أبى هند أنه الموحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are Gabriel's answer: revelation had paused after the Prophet was asked about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; pagans said his Lord had abandoned him, and Gabriel explained he descends only when commanded. The verse and Sura al-Duha were revealed.
rows.anchor: قال له عليه الصلاة والسلام : يا جبريل احتبست عنى حتى ساء ضنى واشتقت اليك فقالك انى كنت اشوق

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji sees this as one story linked to the preceding narrative.
rows.anchor: فهو من عطف القصة على القصة على ما قاله الخفاجي

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: After consoling the Prophet through earlier prophets and contrasting righteous successors with corrupt ones, the passage answers the pagans' claim and consoles him; angelic submission also links the passage to piety and steadfast worship.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف وجه وقوع ذلك هذا الموقع أنه تعالى لم فرغ من اقاصيص الأنبياء عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: The angel's obedience in movement and stillness prepares the command to worship and persevere, and makes the juxtaposition with the ignorant, unjust human an elegant aside.
rows.anchor: ولهذا صرح بعده بقوله تعالى ( فاعبده واصطبر لاعبادته )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report in Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and others says the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, whereupon this verse was revealed; it may have occurred during the earlier conversation or been revealed repeatedly.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال : قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) لجبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام : ما يمنعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some posit an omitted introduction, this is what Gabriel said, to improve the connection, but the author says it adds no useful meaning.
rows.anchor: أن التقدير هذاوقال جبريل : وما نتنزل الخ وبه يظهر حسن العطف

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash reports a view connecting this speech to Gabriel's earlier words, I am only a messenger of your Lord; the author deems it far from acceptable.
rows.anchor: حكى النقاش عن قوم أن الآية متصلة بقول جبريل عليه السلام أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: التنزل normally means descending gradually, but can mean descent generally; a poetic use of تنزل does not imply gradual motion.
rows.anchor: التنزل النزول على مهل لأنه مطاوع نزل يقال نزلته فتنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is that Gabriel and the angels descend from time to time only at God's command, in accordance with His wisdom.
rows.anchor: والمعنى مانتنزل وقتا غب وقت إلا بأمر الله تعالى على ما تقتضية حكمته

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-A'raj reads وما تنزل with a masculine verb; context and occasion identify its subject as revelation, and the speaker remains Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج ( وما تنزل ) بالياء والضمير الموحى بقرينة الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard interpretation takes what is before us as future time, behind us as past, and between as the present; angels descend in every time only by God's leave.
rows.anchor: ما قدامنا من الزمان المستقبل ( وما خلفنا ( من الزمان الماضي

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj maps the three phrases to time before creation, the period after death through the hereafter, and the span of life.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : ما بين الايدي هو ما مر من الزمان فبل الايجاد وما خلف هو ما بعد موتهم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya interprets them as the world until the first Trumpet, the hereafter from resurrection, and the forty years between the two blasts.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية : ما بين الايدي الدنيا بأسرها إلى النفخة الأولى وما خلف ذلك الاخرة

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس، ابن جبير، قتادة، مقاتل، سفيان
rows.claim: The account in al-Tahrir wa al-Tahbir, also narrated from Ibn Abbas and others, identifies what is before as the hereafter and what is behind as the world.
rows.anchor: ورواه العوفى عن ابن عباس وبه قال ابن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل وسفيان

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash takes the phrases as before creation, after extinction, and the interval between this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش : ما بين الايدي هو ما قبل الخلق وما خلف هو ما بعد الفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views interpret the phrases spatially as sky, earth, intervening space, or destination, origin, and present location; some generalize to both space and time, all owned by God, so movement requires His permission.
rows.anchor: واختار بعضهم تفسيرها بما يعم الزمان والمكان والمراد أنه تعالى المالك لكل ذلك

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the phrase means God knows all that is before, behind, and between; therefore angels do not act contrary to His wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي : المراد له علم ما بين ايدينا الخ أي فلا نقدم على مالم يكن موافق حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation generalizes the phrase to God's ownership and knowledge of everything.
rows.anchor: واختار بعضهم التعميم أي له سبحانه ذلك ملكا وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما كان ربك نسيا means God did not abandon His prophets, especially Muhammad; the delayed descent only means no command had been given, not that God forsook him, and this best fits the occasion.
rows.anchor: أي تارك أنبياءه عليهم السلام ويدخل ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) في ذلك دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, نسيا is literal: God's encompassing knowledge and dominion exclude forgetfulness, and the delay arose from wisdom; some prefer this as the intensive form and literal wording fit it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : النسيان على ظاهره يعنى أنه سبحانه لاحاطة علمه وملكه لا يطرأ عليه الغفلة والنسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author selects the non-abandonment explanation because it better suits the reported occasion; the alternative better fits the intensive form and preserves the literal sense, though he questions that rationale.
rows.anchor: واختير الأول لأن هذا المعنى لا يجوز عليه سبحانه فلا حاجة إلى نفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating رب in ربك honors the Prophet, evokes his Lord's care, and signals the reason for the ruling.
rows.anchor: وفي اعادة اسم الرب المعرب عن تبليغ إلى الكمال اللائق مضافا إلى ضميره

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم، ابن بحر
rows.claim: They take the first part through وما بين ذلك as the pious speaking on entering Paradise; their descent means receiving Paradise as a home by God's command and grace, with God owning past, present, and future.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم وابن بحر : أول الآية إلى ( وما بين ذلك ) من كلام المتقين

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم، ابن بحر
rows.claim: On their reading, وما كان ربك نسيا confirms that God does not forget the workers' reward or their deeds as He promised.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم وابن بحر : أول الآية إلى ( وما بين ذلك ) من كلام المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious-speakers reading departs from the apparent sense, leaves ربك addressed to the Prophet unexplained, conflicts with the occasion, and seems chosen only to connect this passage to what precedes.
rows.anchor: حمل التنزل على ما ذكر خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of the heavens and earth explains why forgetfulness is impossible: the owner of all cannot neglect His chosen messenger; رب is either a predicate of an omitted subject or apposition to ربك.
rows.anchor: بيان لاستحالة النسيان عليه تعالى من بيده ملكوت السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative فاعبده follows from God's complete lordship, or from His not abandoning the Prophet or forgetting people's deeds; knowing His lordship entails worship and endurance.
rows.anchor: لترتيب ما بعدها من موجب الأمرين على ما قبلها من كونه تعالى رب السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command also reassures the Prophet not to grieve over delayed revelation or unbelievers' words, since God watches over and cares for him.
rows.anchor: ولا تحزن بابطاء الوحي وكلام الكفرة فانه سبحانه يراقبك ويراعيك

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء، الأخفش
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows رب السماوات to be a subject and فاعبده its predicate, with an extra فاء according to al-Akhfash; the author calls this implausible.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون ( رب السموات ) مبتدأ والخبر ( فاعبده ) والفاء زائده

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows وما كان ربك نسيا to continue the pious people's speech only if رب is a predicate of an omitted subject, not if it is apposition.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن يكون قوله تعالى : ( وما كان ربك نسيا ) من تتمة كلام المتقين

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf argues that making the command a response to an omitted condition about knowing Paradise's state weakens the eloquence by leaving the obvious cause.
rows.anchor: لا يلائم كما في الكشف فصاحة التنزيل للعدول عن السبب الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اصطبر is paired with ل rather than the usual على because it conveys standing firm through hardships encountered in worship, like a fighter holding against an opponent.
rows.anchor: لتضمنه معنى الثبات للعبادة فيما تورد عليه من الشدائد والمشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wording signals the struggle of worship and steadfastness, with an allusion to the saying about returning from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad.
rows.anchor: وشمة من معنى رجعنا من الجهاد الأصغر إلى الجهاد الأكبر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، ابن جبير، قتادة
rows.claim: They explain سمي as an equal or match; because sharing a name implies likeness, it can mean a counterpart. Ibn Atiyya similarly glosses it as one equal or parallel.
rows.anchor: أي مثلا كما جاء في رواية جماعة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations specify a partner in the name Lord of the heavens and earth, in the divine name Allah, in Allah or al-Rahman, or in the name God in its true sense rather than a false attribution.
rows.anchor: أن يراد ههنا الشريك في اسم خاص قد عبر عنه تعالى بذلك وهو رب السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, when asked by Nafi ibn al-Azraq, interprets سمي as a child; the same view is reported from al-Dahhak and supported with a poetic line.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الطستى عن ابن عباس أن نافع ابن الازرق سأله عن ذلك فقال : السمي الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever interpretation is adopted, denying knowledge of a match emphatically denies that any match exists; the question establishes the duty to worship God.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بانكار العلم ونفيه إنكار المعلوم ونفيه على أبلغ وجه واكده والجملة تقرير

rows.speaker: الكسائي، هشام، علي بن نصر، هارون عن أبي عمرو، الحسن، الأعمش، عيسى، ابن محيصن
rows.claim: They assimilate the ل into ت in هتعلم; Abu Ubayda says this is a dialect alongside clear pronunciation, and a line by Muzahim al-Uqayli witnesses the form هتعين.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وهشام وعلي بن نصر وهرون كلاهما عن أبى عمرو والحسن والأعمش

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the verse was revealed about al-Asi ibn Wa'il; other reported candidates are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج انها نزلت في العاصي بن وائل

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira as the person meant; another view names Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء عن ابن عباس انها نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says it concerns Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who crumbled a decayed bone, scattered it, and denied that resurrection after death could happen.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي انها في أبى ابن خلف اخذ عظما باليا فجعل يفته بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإنسان may denote one of the named individuals or a particular group of unbelievers who deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: فال في ( الانسان ) على ما قيل للعهد والمراد به أحد هؤلاء الأشخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the generic noun can mean some members of humanity, either by whole-for-part usage or by predicating a few people's act of the whole; a poetic example illustrates the latter.
rows.anchor: وقال غير واحد : يجوز أن تكون ال للجلس ويكون هناك مجاز في الطرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians require the rest of a group to approve or assist for an act to be attributed to all; one answer says denial is rooted in everyone's nature before examining evidence.
rows.anchor: واعترض هذا بأنه يشترط لصحة ذلك الاسناد رضا الباقين بالفعل أو مساعدتهم

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says group consent is not required for valid attribution, only a rhetorical reason; here public denial should have been stopped, so failure to condemn it counts as consent and urges people to oppose it.
rows.anchor: الحق عدم اشتراط ذلك لصحته وإنما يشترط لحسنه نكته يقتضيها مقام الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that generic phrasing highlights how few people believe in resurrection as the truthful revelation describes it, as stated in 12:103.
rows.anchor: إلى قلة المؤمنين بالبعث على الوجه الذي اخبر به الصادق وما اكثر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense either evokes the past scene as strange or denotes repeated speech continuing until the Trumpet is blown.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالمضارع عما استحضارا للصورة الماضية لنوع غرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza precedes an understood verb; إذا is usually temporal, and the phrase has an omitted coordinated clause, meaning when he dies and becomes dust.
rows.anchor: أي ائذا ما مات وصرت رميما لسوف الخ

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya considers سوف to prevent the temporal إذا from attaching to the verb; the author cites a poetic counterexample, while al-Radi analyzes إذا as conditional and most prefer the temporal reading.
rows.anchor: وعد ابن عطية توسط سوف مانعا من العمل ايضا ورد عليه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is emphatic if سوف makes the verb refer to the present; if it does not, no special emphatic-only reading is needed. ما in إذا ما is also emphatic.
rows.anchor: واللام هنا لمجرد التوكيد ولذا ساغ اقترانها بحرف الأستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خرج can mean literal emergence from the earth or metaphorical transition from nonexistence to a new state.
rows.anchor: والمراد من الأخراج الأخراج من الأرض أو من حال العناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time expression is fronted before the verb because the disputed point is resurrection at that time, not resurrection in general; fronting it places the focus of denial at the interrogative hamza.
rows.anchor: وأيلاء الظرف همزة الأنكار دون الأخراج لأن ذلك الأخراج ليس بمنكر مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question can deny that a time will ever come in which life follows death, a stronger denial than rejecting resurrection itself.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد انكار وقت ذلك بعينه أي انكار مجيء وقت فيه حياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some retain no omitted coordinated clause, treating the time of death as extended beyond the instant the soul leaves; others say rejecting resurrection at death already entails rejecting it after decay.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم لم يقدر معطوفا واعتبر زمان الموت ممتدا

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Ibn Dhakwan reportedly reads إذا without the interrogative hamza, either supplied by context or as a mocking declarative statement.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جماعة منهم ابن ذكوان بخلاف عنه ( اذا ) بدون همرة الأستفهام وهي مقدرة معه

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Talha reads سأخرج with the future س and without the lām, so إذا attaches directly to the verb; another report from him reads لساخرج.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف ( سأخرج ) بسين الأستقبال وبغير لام وعلى ذلك تكون إذا متعلقة

rows.speaker: الحسن، أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Hasan and Abu Haywa read أخرج in the active voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابو حيوة ( أخرج ) مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يذكر means reflect; explicit الانسان replaces a pronoun to stress that human nature itself should prompt reflection on its creation and forbid the earlier denial.
rows.anchor: من الذكر الذي يراد به التفكر والأظهار في موضع الاضمار لزيادة التقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is a rebuke with an omitted coordinated clause: does he say this and fail to remember that God created him before, when he was nothing? It may also reject combining the claim with failure to remember.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للانكار التوبيخي وهي على أحد المذهبين المشهورين في مثل هذا التركيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating from nothing is a stronger proof than restoring someone who once existed, whether restoration means returning the same person or gathering dispersed matter and recreating its former accidents.
rows.anchor: فحيث خلقناه وهو في تلك الحاله المنافيه للخلق بالكليه مع كونه ابعد من الوقوع

rows.speaker: غير واحد من السبعة، أبي
rows.claim: Many of the seven readers pronounce يذكر with open ذال and كاف and a doubled consonant, assimilating the ت of يتذكر; Ubayy also reads the assimilated form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ غير واحد من السبعة ( يذكر ) بفتح الذال والكاف وتشديدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by the Prophet's Lord confirms the gathering, honors the Prophet through the possessive address, and implies its cause; gathering the deniers after revival is asserted while revival itself has already been proven.
rows.anchor: مضافا إلى ضميره ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) لتحقيق الأمر بالأشعار بعلته وتفخيم شأنه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: The pronoun most likely refers to the unbelievers who made the preceding denial, though a generic use can refer to humanity while intending one or some members.
rows.anchor: وكون الضمير للكفرة القائلين هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers taking the pronoun as all people, believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: واستظهر أبو حيان أنه للنلس كلهم مؤمنهم وكافرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase جثيا means kneeling on the knees; its dual و structure is altered through phonetic easing, and several readers use the nominative plural form.
rows.anchor: بلركيت على الركب واصله جثوو بواوين

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib allows جثيا to be a verbal noun, like the proposed analysis of بكيا.
rows.anchor: وجوز الراغب كونه مصدرا نظير ما قيل في بكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' being brought kneeling may humiliate them or reflect their inability to stand under the terror.
rows.anchor: ولعل إحضار الكفرة بهذه الحال اهانا لهم أو لعجزهم عن القيام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say people kneel around Hell to dispute during the reckoning, after which some disavow others.
rows.anchor: إن المحاسبه تكون حول جهنم فيجثون لمخاصمة بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says they kneel because the space around Hell is crowded.
rows.anchor: وقال السدى : يجثون لضيق المكان بهم فالحال على القولين مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If all people are gathered, the saved see what God spared them from and rejoice, while the damned face their deeds and become more enraged at the saved; kneeling may follow terror, crowding, or the reckoning before judgment.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل الضمير للكفرة وغيرهم قال : أنه يحضر السعداء والأشقياء حول جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that everyone kneels to display humility in that dreadful place; 45:28 describes every nation as kneeling, though later reports may show not all are.
rows.anchor: وقيل أنهم يجثون على ركبهم اظهارا للذل في ذلك الموطن العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical state is variously taken as prospective or actual; it cannot consistently be prospective for the saved and actual for the damned.
rows.anchor: والحال قيل : مقدرة وقيل : غير مقدرة إلا أنه اسند ما للبعض إلى الكل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets جثيا as groups, from جثو meaning collected earth or stones.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنه فسر ( جثيا ) بجماعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شيعة can mean a group cooperating in or following falsehood, as the passage concerns unbelievers, or any group sharing a religion if all people are addressed.
rows.anchor: أي جماعه تشايعة وتعاونة على الباطل أو شاعة وتبعت الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عتيا means turning away from obedience and rebelling; Ibn Abbas glosses it as audacity, Mujahid as disbelief, and another view as slander in Tamim speech; most favor the first meaning.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس جراءة وعن مجاهد كفرا وقيل : افتراء بلغة تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عتيا is a verbal noun under the established readings; the claim that it is a plural of جاث is unlikely here.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على التفسير الأول وهو على سائر التفاسير مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نزع means extracting, as in 28:32; the action proceeds repeatedly, selecting the most rebellious from each group until all are gathered, then casting them into Hell in order of desert.
rows.anchor: والنزع الأخراج كما في قوله تعالى ( ونزع يده ) والمراد استمرار ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extracted members are brought forward in sequence, beginning with those most deserving of punishment.
rows.anchor: فاذا اجتمعوا طرحناهم في النار على الترتيب نقدم أولاهم بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those most entitled to burn can mean the extracted individuals in order, or the whole set considered together as the most entitled among wrongdoers; their burning is expressed in place of a pronoun.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالذين هم أولى المنتزعون باعتبار الترتيب وقد يراد بهم أولئك باعتبار المجموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation takes نزع as shooting an arrow: the most rebellious of each faction are shot into the Fire first, and then God knows their burning.
rows.anchor: وفسر بعضهم النزع بالرمى من نزعت السهم عن القوس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The ordering that begins with the most rebellious is also transmitted from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: وحمل الآية على البداء بالأشد فالأشد مروى عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, in a report from Ibn Abi Hatim, says the most rebellious are the sects' leaders and imams, whose crime is multiplied because they mislead others; 16:88 and 29:13 support this.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ذلك ابن أبى حاتم عن قتادة وعليه لا يجب الأستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that a universal reading makes everyone share in rebellion is answered by attributing a trait of some to a whole group; a superlative over a class need not describe each member, and singling out the worst hints at mercy toward many.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عنه بأن ذلك من نيبة ما للبعض إلى الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preferred grammatical parse, أيهم is the object of ننزعن, a relative pronoun in the accusative; أشد predicates an omitted subject, while عتيا is a transferred specification.
rows.anchor: و ( أيهم ) مفعول ( ننزعن ) وهو اسم موصول بمعنى الذي مبنى على الضم محله النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على الرحمن may modify أشد or explain it; بها and صليا admit parallel analyses, with the latter read in both damma and kasra and analyzed as a verbal noun or adjective.
rows.anchor: ( وعلى الرحمن ) متعلق بأشد ( وعتيا ) تمييز محول عن المبتدأ

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets الصلى as entering the Fire, while Ibn Jurayj interprets it as remaining there forever; neither is its strictly literal meaning.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبى أنه فسر الصلى بالدخول وعن ابن جريج أنه فسره بالخلود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form and case of أي are disputed: Sibawayh builds it on damma here because the head of its clause is omitted, while many grammarians reject that analysis.
rows.anchor: وكان حقها أن تبنى في كل موضع كسائر الموصولات

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الجرمي
rows.claim: Abu Amr al-Jarmi says that from Basra to Mecca he heard no one use Sibawayh's form لأضربن أيهم قائم with أيهم in the nominative.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو الجرمى فخرجت من البصرة فلم اسمع منذ فارقت الخندق إلى مكة احدا يقول

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says he knows of no grammarian who did not regard Sibawayh as mistaken on this question.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر : النحاس ما علمت احدا من النحويين إلا وقد خطأ سيبويه في هذه المسئلة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says only two passages in Sibawayh's book appear mistaken, and this is one of them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : ما تبين أن سيبويه غلط في كتابه إلا في موضعين هذا احدهما

rows.speaker: علاء الدين
rows.claim: Al-Alusi's teacher, Ala al-Din, defended Sibawayh at length, but the author says the defense does not merit recounting.
rows.anchor: وقد تكلف شيخنا علاء الدين علا الله تعالى مقامه في عليين للذب عن سيبويه

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف، معاذ بن مسلم، زائدة عن الأعمش
rows.claim: Their accusative reading أيهم supports Sibawayh's object analysis, though it challenges his insistence on building the form when annexed and its clause head is omitted.
rows.anchor: قراءة طلحة بن مصرفومعاذ بن مسلم الهراء استاذ الفراء وزائدة عن الأعمش ( أيهم ) بالنصب

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil makes the object of نزع an omitted relative pronoun and treats أيهم أشد as an interrogative clause in reported speech; the author objects that extracting those asked about makes little sense.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل : مفعول ( ننزعن ) موصول محذوف واى هنا استفهامية مبتدأ وأشد خبره

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Defenders say the extraction is figurative because their degrees of rebellion are close, or means those identified by the answer; the author calls the required omissions excessive and nonproductive.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن ذلك مجاز عن تقارب احوالهم وتشابهها في العتو

rows.speaker: الكسائي، الفراء، المهدوي
rows.claim: They follow al-Khalil but place the interrogative clause as the accusative object of extraction, meaning those who answer the question; they justify suspension as with verbs of knowing or calling.
rows.anchor: وذهب الكسائى والفراء إلى ماقاله الخليل إلا انهما جعلا الجمله في محل نصب

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus allows suspension by an interrogative with verbs of every kind, not just a limited class.
rows.anchor: ويونس لا يراى التعليق مختصا بصنف من الأفعال بل سائر اصنافها سواء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Another parse treats the question as independent and lets the verb govern كل شيعة, with من extra in an affirmative statement or interpreted as a partitive; the author notes the readings require interpretive additions or depart from the apparent single clause.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الجملة الاستفهامية استئنافية والفعل واقع على ( كل شيعة ) على زيادة من

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad is reported to make أيهم the subject of شيعة because شيعة means follow; another version says it attaches to شيعة as a description of followers, but requires an omitted object for نزع.
rows.anchor: ونقل بعضهم عن المبرد أن ( أيهم ) غاعل ( شيعة ) لأن معناه يشيع

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن شقير، أبو حيان
rows.claim: A Kufi grammarian takes أيهم conditionally, as whether they rebel or not; Abu Hayyan considers this implausible.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو بكر بن شقير أن بعض الكوفيين يقول في أيهم معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most natural reading is Sibawayh's; syntax judgments ultimately rest on attested usage, and the lack of another attestation does not disprove the one heard.
rows.anchor: والوجه الذي ينساق اليه الذهن ويساعده اللفظ والمعنى هو ما ذهب اليه سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts to مخاطب humanity or the specific deniers to intensify attention; another view sees a fresh divine address after the earlier point is complete, while a reading has منهم instead of منكم.
rows.anchor: التفات إلى خطاب الانسان سواء اريد منه العموم أو خصوص الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many early exegetes and Sunnis take الورود as entering Hell, supported by the statement that worshippers and what they worship are its fuel and Pharaoh brings his people into it; Ibn Abbas used these verses against Ibn al-Azraq.
rows.anchor: أي دخلها كما ذهب إلى ذلك جمع كثير من سلف المفسرين وأهل السنة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report judged sound by al-Hakim, Jaber swears he heard the Prophet say every righteous and wicked person enters Hell; it is cool and safe for believers as it was for Abraham, then God saves the pious.
rows.anchor: فلقيت جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنه فذكرت له فقال : واهوى باصبعيه إلى اذنيه

rows.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: They interpret الورود as passing over Hell without entering, across the bridge placed above it, as also transmitted from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن الأنبارى والبيهقى عن الحسن الورود المرور عليها من غير دخول

rows.speaker: خالد بن معدان
rows.claim: Khalid says Paradise's people will ask about the promised passage through Hell; God answers that they crossed while it was extinguished, which does not conflict with a report where Hell addresses the believer because he may not remember or have heard it.
rows.anchor: عن خالد بن معدان قال : إذا دخل أهل الجنة الجنة قالوا : ربنا الم تعدنا أن نرد النار

rows.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Hell tells the believer to pass because his light has extinguished its flame; this can coexist with the other report.
rows.anchor: عن يعلى ابن امية عن النبى ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) أنه قال : تقول النار للمؤمن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd distinguishes believers' passing over the bridge from unbelievers' entry; this requires a general metaphor if one word cannot bear both senses.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبى حاتم عن ابن زيد أنه قال في الآية ورود المسلمين المرور على الجسر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the believer's ورود is fever touching the body in this world, citing the report that fever comes from Hell's breath; the author says the inference is tenuous.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أن ورود المؤمن النار هو مس الحمى جسده في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra about the Prophet visiting a sick companion says God makes fever a believer's share of fire in this life; it does not show that the person will not encounter Hell after death.
rows.anchor: بما أخرجه ابن جرير عن أبى هريرة قال : خرج رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) يعود رجلا

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr interprets ورود as presence or nearness, as when Moses arrived at the water of Midian; some choose this for everyone's coming near Hell and kneeling around it.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد ابن حميد عن عبيد بن عمير أن الورود الحضور والقرب كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction with those kept far from Hell: they are far from its punishment, or are removed after first coming near it.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة بين هذه الآية وقوله تعالى ( أولئك عنها مبعدون ) لأن المراد مبعدون عن عذابها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The phrase حتما مقضيا means a decided, certain decree; describing it as obligatory means inevitable occurrence, since Sunnis hold nothing is obligatory upon God.
rows.anchor: على ربك حتما ( اورا واجبا كما روى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عكرمة، ابن مسعود، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: Ikrima, Ibn Masud, Hasan, and Qatada explain حتما مقضيا as an obligatory oath; some see it as initiating an oath, with على ربك carrying the oath sense, supported by Arabic poetry and oath idioms.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الخطيب عن عكرمة أن معنى كان حتما مقضيا كان قسما واجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explains the Prophet's saying that a Muslim whose three children die will not enter Hell except as a slight fulfillment of the oath.
rows.anchor: لا يموت لمسلم ثلاثة من الولد فيلج النار إلا تحلة القسم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة، ابن عطية
rows.claim: They say the hadith's reference to an oath alludes to the oath at the beginning of the verse, and some parse the verse's و as an oath particle.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وابن عطية وتبعهما غير واحد : أن القسم في الخبر أشارة إلى القسم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that grammarians do not allow an oath wāw with its governed noun omitted except in rare or poetic usage, and an oath answer cannot be omitted here under their rules.
rows.anchor: لا يذهب نحوى إلى ان مثل الواو واو القسم لأنه يلزم من ذلك حذف المجرور

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham treats تحلة القسم as an idiom for a small amount, supported by a poetic example; al-Khafaji allows a circumstantial or coordinated parse, but the author finds the idiomatic reading safest.
rows.anchor: وجعل ابن هشام تحله القسم كناية عن القلة

rows.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
rows.claim: A report says a volunteer guarding the Muslims' rear does not see Hell except slightly; the author says it fits the idiom because universal entry must occur.
rows.anchor: من حرس من وراء المسلمين في سبيل الله تعالى متطوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's causal explanation remains valid if تحلة القسم means a little: because everyone must encounter Hell as God declared, otherwise a guard might never see it at all.
rows.anchor: فان التعليل صحيح مع ارادة القلة من ذلك أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious are saved by being taken out of Hell, while the wrongdoers remain kneeling, as reported from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd; this strongly indicates الورود means entry.
rows.anchor: بالأخراج منها على ماذهب اليه الجمع الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take this as evidence that everyone merely kneels near Hell, with the two clauses detailing that state; the author objects that no implied phrase meaning around Hell is needed and kneeling does not prove nearness.
rows.anchor: وانت تعلم أن الظاهر عدم التقدير والجثو لايوجب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrasting the pious with wrongdoers emphasizes mercy: even minimal piety, namely avoiding shirk, saves, while persistent polytheism destroys; نذر also suggests casting something away as negligible.
rows.anchor: ليؤذن بترجيح جانب الرحمه وان التوحيد هو المنجي والاشراك هو المردى

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi says ثم signals a temporal and rank difference between the creaturely act of entering Hell and God's act of rescue and destruction.
rows.anchor: وجئ بثم للايذان بالتفاوت بين فعل الخلق وهو ورودهم النار

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report in al-Tirmidhi says sinful monotheists are burned to charcoal, then mercy removes them and Paradise's people sprinkle water until they grow like flood debris; rescue occurs successively according to piety, down to a grain of good.
rows.anchor: يعذب ناس من أهل التوحد في النار حتى يكونوا حمما ثم تدركهم الرحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that fire does not harm a believer is understood of the fully faithful, since many reports say some believers are punished for their sins.
rows.anchor: وما ظاهره من الأخبار كخبر جابر السابق أن المؤمن لاتضره النار مؤول

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars prohibit prayers asking that every member of Muhammad's community be forgiven all sins or that none be punished, given reports of punishment for sinners.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا حظر بعض العلماء أن يقال في الدعاء : اللهم اغفر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: If the address is only to unbelievers, the rescued pious are led from the brink of Hell to Paradise, with ثم contrasting humiliation and honor; the author notes only the elect avoid entering Hell entirely.
rows.anchor: ان المراد من التنجيه على تقدير أن الخطاب خاص بالكفرة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites restrict the pious to those without grave sins, classify major sinners as wrongdoers, and infer from the verse that they remain eternally in Hell.
rows.anchor: والمعتزلة خصوا الذين اتقوا بغير اصحاب الكبائر وادخلوهم في الضالمين

rows.speaker: علي، ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، أبي، الجحدري، معاذ بن قرة، يعقوب
rows.claim: They read ثم with an open ث, meaning there; Ibn Abi Layla adds a pausal ه, and the adverb modifies what follows.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن عباس وابن مسعود وابى رضى الله تعالى عنهم والجحدرى ومعاة ية بن قرة ويعقوب ( ثم ) بفتح الثاء

rows.speaker: يحيى، الأعمش، الكسائي، ابن محيصم، يعقوب
rows.claim: They read ننجى with a light ج; other variants use passive forms with or without doubling, a one-nun form with doubled ج, and Ali's ننحى with ح, which supports interpreting الورود as nearness or presence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى والأعمش والكسائى وابن محيصم ويعقوب ( ننجى ) بتخفيف الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage reports what the polytheists said after hearing signs exposing their shameful state and outcome; the signs include the preceding verses and are clear either in miraculous inimitability or in wording, meaning, and explained purposes.
rows.anchor: إلى اخرها حكاية لما قالوا عند سماع الآيات الناعية عليهم فظاعة حالهم ووخامة ما لهم

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf prefers بَيِّنَات as a circumstantial qualifier that reinforces the whole statement, despite the clause not having two nominal parts.
rows.anchor: والوجه كما في الكشاف أن يكون ( بينات ) حالا مؤكدة لمضمون الجملة

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة، الأعرج، ابن محيصن
rows.claim: They read وإذا يتلى with a masculine verb because آيات is metaphorically feminine and separated from the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن ( وإذا يتلى ) بالياء التحتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative description الذين كفروا highlights that their statement came from people rejecting the revelation, or specifically hardened leaders such as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his followers, about whom the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: ووضع الموصول موضع الضمير للتنبيه على أنهم قالوا ما قالوا كافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ل in للذين آمنوا is communicative, as in telling someone something; a causal reading, for their sake or about them, is less fitting because the question compares both groups.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله تعالى ( للذين آمنوا ( للتبليغ كما في قلت له كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أي الفريقين means which group, us or you, has the better place; مقام broadly denotes residence or location, while the nominative reading can suggest a place of dwelling.
rows.anchor: كانهم قالوا : اينا ( خير ( نحن اوانتم ( مقاما ( أي مكانا ومنزلا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، ابن محيصن، حميد، الجعفي، أبو حاتم عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: They read مقاما with a damma on the م, from إقامة, meaning a place of residence; it agrees in sense with the open-vowel reading.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد والجعفي وابوا حاتم عن أبى عمرو ( مقاما ) بضم الاميم

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr allows both vowelings to be verbal nouns, respectively from قام and أقام.
rows.anchor: وجوز في البحر احتمال المفتوح والمضموم للمصدرية

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: A distinction attributed to Abu al-Su'ud makes the open form any place of standing, temporary or lasting, while the damma form is where one is established by another or remains for an extended time.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الأول يعنى المفتوح الميم موضع قيام الشئ اعم من أن يكون قيامه فيه بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a quadriliteral verb specifically means an externally established or enduring place, the damma form is the required one.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا قصد ذلك فان مقتضاه الثاني كما إذا قلت

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: The account distinguishes original lexical standing from later usage: the former is a place something stands by itself, while the latter is like a necessary station for a volitional being; with a quadriliteral verb, a verbal noun takes damma.
rows.anchor: ومقامات الكلمات كلها وان كانت منوطه بوضع الوضع لكن مفامها المنوط باصل الوضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text concludes that مقام in this verse is a tamyiz, not an adverbial or verbal noun; its sense is which group's position is better.
rows.anchor: وانت تعلم أنه في هذا المقام ليس منصوبا على الظرفية ولا على المصدرية بل منصوب على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نديا means a council or gathering; al-Bahr specifies a meeting for discussion or consultation, while another view connects it with generosity.
rows.anchor: أي مجلسا ومجتمعا وفي البحر هو المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه لحادثه أو مشورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers reportedly groomed and perfumed themselves, wore their finest clothes, and taunted poor believers with their superior social setting.
rows.anchor: يروى أنهم كانوا يرجلون شعورهم ويدهنوها ويتطيبون ويلبسون مفاخر الملابس

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains their argument: if believers were right, a wise God would not leave His sincere allies in hardship while disbelievers enjoyed comfort; the inference is invalid and based on a foolish view, as the next verse refutes it.
rows.anchor: قال الأمام : ومرادهم من ذلك معارضت المؤمنين كانهم قالوا لوا كنتم على الحق
